title: What Flight Deck should do now, as a step toward the future loop
from: Flight Deck and the future-of-product research, together
description: Four choices about what Flight Deck does for a product person today, each chosen so it also moves toward the future-of-product loop.
why: You asked for Flight Deck and the future-of-product work to line up. They work on different horizons: the research is a vision of where product work is going, and Flight Deck has to be useful to a product person today. So this is **not a scorecard** of truths covered. Each choice asks what helps someone now and also takes a step toward the loop. Things that only make sense once the future arrives, such as always-on sensing or steward agents, are marked later, and that's fine. The [mapping](https://github.com/dudgeon/flight-deck-demo/blob/claude/vision-mapping/docs/vision/mapping.md) has the detail. Both sides agreed this brief.

Both sides now use three artifact names and avoid "spec" and "PRD": the **statement of intent** (the person's short account of the change, outcome, risk and what would prove it wrong), the **solution design** (drafted by agents and settled by people: how it fits the platforms, its dependencies and the alternatives) and the **decision record**.
how_to_answer: Pick an option on each decision, or Something else, and add a note if you like. Picks save to this page as you go. Send answers to Claude when you're done.
recommendation: Keep Flight Deck's arcs, tag each with the moves it serves, and rename our tier called "move", since you use that word for the loop. Build first the things that help today and also lead toward the loop: statement-of-intent fields (risk accepted, what would prove it wrong) and a Challenge option that argues the other side. Rename the "PRD to dependencies" arc after what it produces, the solution design, and split the template so the statement of intent stays short. Turn the rewards story into an invented-company scenario whose moves become the first quality evals, and keep the original local.

findings.title: Decide, the trail and status are covered.
findings.body: Decision briefs and the Decisions register, initiative registers with stamped artifacts, and the delivery status update already do what the decide and learn moves and truth 12 need, up to where code starts.

findings.title: Investigate works today; constant sensing is later.
findings.body: Problem discovery synthesises the sources a person brings, with checked quotes. Watching signals unasked belongs to the future, not to what's missing today.

findings.title: Prototype is designed, challenge is missing.
findings.body: The Prototype move and a default enterprise prototyper that takes channel teams' design-system packs are designed (PR 54) but not built. Nothing argues the other side on purpose. Review gets second opinions on a document, which is close but not the same.

findings.title: One template holds two artifacts.
findings.body: The initiative-intent template mixes the statement of intent (goal, problem, customer, outcome, scope) with the solution design (approach, dependencies, delivery). It has no field for the risk accepted or what would prove it wrong.

findings.title: Five moves are platform work.
findings.body: Build, verify, release, replays and simulations, and steward agents belong to the enterprise's delivery, data and risk platforms. Flight Deck is the person's side: it hands intent over and records decisions.

findings.title: Only routing has evals.
findings.body: The routing suite checks whether Aviator starts or offers the right work. Nothing yet measures whether a skill does its move well.

findings.title: Flight Deck assumes a PM; truth 3 doesn't.
findings.body: Flight Deck's framing and copy are written for product managers. Truth 3 says product judgment spreads to whoever is closest to the problem, and your own edit to the rewards story made its lead "a builder on the Rewards team". Not a decision here: the rename work in FP-1 can cover the copy too if you want.

findings.title: Specify works on the solution design.
findings.body: The "PRD to dependencies" arc (Specify, Map, Choose) produces most of a solution design: requirements traced to lines, dependencies, alternatives. So it doesn't lengthen the statement of intent, and the earlier clash with truth 7 was only a naming problem.

decisions.label: FP-1
decisions.question: Should Flight Deck stay organised as a line of arcs, or around the eleven moves?
context: Flight Deck's arcs run in lifecycle order (Discover, Shape, Specify, Engage, Deliver) and allow going back. The research's moves loop many times before a bet, and you told it that linear reads as wrong. Both are in front of the same person, so the two should agree.
know: Flight Deck also calls Review and Decide "moves" (a tier: done to any artifact). You use "moves" for the loop yourself, so Flight Deck's tier is the one to rename.
Changing the Library's organisation means reworking the taxonomy, routing and the routing evals.
Moves map many-to-many onto arcs: problem discovery alone serves sense and investigate.

stage.caption: The arcs a person starts from, or the moves they make

options.label: Keep the arcs and tag each with its moves
options.cost: Small: a field per workflow and a docs pass
options.consequence: A person still starts from five named arcs; each says which moves it serves, and the mapping stays readable. Our tier called "move" is renamed (for example "action") so the word means one thing. The Library still reads as a sequence.

options.label: Organise around the moves
options.cost: Large: taxonomy, Library, routing and evals reworked
options.consequence: The Library matches the loop exactly, and gaps show as empty moves. It drops the stage model that initiatives and the companion are built on.

options.label: Leave both as they are
options.consequence: No work now. The two describe the same person's work differently, and the word "move" keeps two meanings.

decisions.reason: Tagging keeps what is built and makes the loop visible where it matters, without rebuilding routing while both sides are still changing.

decisions.label: FP-2
decisions.question: Which should Flight Deck build first, useful today and a step toward the loop?
context: These are the gaps a person's workspace could close. Platform work is left out.
know: Hypothesis fields are a template and checklist change. Challenge can start as an option on the Review move.
The Prototype move is already designed (PR 54): one contract, routed by channel, a default prototyper that takes design-system packs, and platform teams can ship their own. It's the largest to build.

stage.caption: What a harness could close

options.label: Hypothesis fields and Challenge
options.consequence: Shaping produces a falsifiable bet, and any hypothesis can be attacked on purpose: the strongest case for each rival explanation, the evidence that would separate them, and a check for bias in that evidence (in the rewards story, whether only engaged customers find a hidden feature). That is more than a second opinion on a document. Prototyping waits.

options.label: Prototype move first
options.consequence: The most visible demo of truth 5, testing and describing converging. Bigger, and the bet it prototypes still has no falsifier.

options.label: Standing discovery first
options.consequence: Problems surface unasked, which truth 1 leans on. It's mostly a future capability, and a demo would have to invent the signals to watch.

decisions.reason: Both help a product person today, since a sharper bet and a deliberate counter-argument are useful in any team. Both also build the human-judgment moves the loop puts first, and they make the evals in FP-3 possible.

decisions.label: FP-3
decisions.question: Should the rewards story become a Flight Deck scenario, with its moves as the first quality evals?
context: Flight Deck runs demo stories called scenarios, with invented data. The research's rewards story walks every move. It's set at a real kind of business and stays local by your earlier call, and Flight Deck is a public repo.
know: An invented company and invented customers would keep the moves and drop anything specific to the original setting.
Each move in the story would become an eval task: does the skill do that move well.

stage.caption: The research keeps the original; Flight Deck flies a copy

options.label: Yes, an invented-company version
options.cost: One scenario and an eval suite
options.consequence: One story tests both sides: the research checks its truths against it, Flight Deck demos and measures its skills on it. The two versions can drift and need a check now and then.

options.label: Wait for more scenarios
options.consequence: Nothing duplicated while the research keeps rewriting. Flight Deck's evals stay routing-only for now.

options.label: Flight Deck writes its own scenarios
options.consequence: Flight Deck's demos stay independent of the research, and the two may test different things.

decisions.reason: It joins the two pieces of work at one point and gives Flight Deck its first measure of skill quality.

decisions.label: FP-4
decisions.question: Should the "PRD to dependencies" arc and its Specify step be renamed after the solution design?
context: You asked that neither side use "spec" or "PRD". The arc and its first step carry both words, though what they produce is a solution design.
know: The arc was named in D-148 and is being built in PR 54, so a rename now costs little.
Splitting the intent template into a statement of intent and a solution design goes with this either way.

stage.caption: Same steps, named for what they produce

options.label: Rename it "Solution design", Specify becomes Requirements
options.cost: A rename in PR 54 and the docs
options.consequence: The arc says what it produces, and both sides use the same three artifact names. Existing routing examples and copy that say "PRD" get reworded. A person can still start from a document they call a PRD.

options.label: Rename only the Specify step
options.consequence: The arc keeps a name people at work recognise, so it's easier to find from a PRD in hand. The word you asked to avoid stays on the Library.

options.label: Keep both names
options.consequence: No change, but the arc's name contradicts the shared vocabulary.

decisions.reason: It costs least while PR 54 is open, and it ends the naming clash that made the last tension.

after: Flight Deck records your answers as decisions in its repo and builds what you pick. The research updates its moves, artifacts and asset list to match. If you change the truths or moves later, the research tells Flight Deck what changed and the mapping follows.
